problems.title: Question 4
problems.problem:
[14 marks]

It is well known that the temperature of a closed room goes up if the refrigerator is switched on inside it. A refrigerator compartment set to temperature $T_C$ is turned on inside a hut in Leh (Ladakh). The atmosphere (outside the hut) can be considered to be a vast reservoir at constant temperature $T_O$. Walls of hut and refrigerator compartment are conducting. The temperature of the refrigerator compartment is maintained at $T_C$ with the help of a compressor engine. We explain the working of the refrigerator engine and the heat flow with the help of the associated figure.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/inpho-2014-4-fig1.png

The larger square is the refrigerator compartment with heat leak per unit time $Q_C$ into it from the room. The same heat per unit time $Q_C$ is pumped out of it by the engine (also called compressor and indicated by the smaller square in thick). The compressor does work $W$ and rejects heat per unit time $Q_H$ into the hut. The thermal conductance (in units of watt per kelvin) of the walls of the compartment and hut respectively are $K_C$ and $K_H$. After a long time it is found that temperature of the hut is $T_H$. The compressor works as a reverse Carnot engine and it does not participate in heat conduction process.

(a) [3½ marks] State the law of heat conduction for the walls of the hut and the refrigerator compartment.

(b) [3½ marks] We define the dimensionless quantities $k = K_H/K_C$, $h = T_H/T_O$ and $c = T_C/T_O$. Express $h$ is terms of $c$ and $k$.

(c) [3 marks] Calculate stable temperature $T_H$ given $T_O = 280.0\,\mathrm{K}$, $T_C = 252.0\,\mathrm{K}$ and $k = 0.90$.

(d) [2 marks] Now another identical refrigerator is put inside the hut. $T_C$ and $T_O$ do not change but $T_H$, the hut temperature will change to $T_H'$. State laws of heat conduction for hut and one of the two identical refrigerator compartments.

(e) [2 marks] Assume that the dimensionless quantities $k$ and $c$ do not change. Let $h' = T_H'/T_O$. Obtain an expression for $h'$.

Find approximately the ratio of the speed ($v_o$) that the cart would acquire if all men jump one after the other to the speed ($v_a$) that it would acquire if all of them jump simultaneously off the cart. There is no friction between the cart and the ground.

Hint: In calculating the value of the ratio, you should make use of the fact there are a large number of men.

problems.title: Question 7: Bohr-Wheeler fission limit
problems.problem:
[13 marks]

Using the liquid drop model for the nucleus, Bohr and Wheeler established in 1939 a natural limit for $Z^2/A$ beyond which nuclei are unstable against spontaneous fission, where $Z$ and $A$ are the atomic and nucleon numbers respectively. In the following problem we will estimate this limit.

Consider the liquid drop model of a nucleus where the total energy of the nucleus is considered to be sum of surface energy $U_A$ and electrostatic energy $U_E$. $U_A$ can be expressed as $U_A = a_S R^2$ where $a_S$ is a dimensioned proportionality constant and $R$ is the radius of the nucleus. In what follows we take the nucleus to be spherical with its radius $R = r_0 A^{1/3}$ where $r_0 = 1.2\,\mathrm{fm}$ ($1\,\mathrm{fm} = 10^{-15}\,\mathrm{m}$). Consider the case of a nucleus of radius $R_0$, atomic mass $A$ and atomic number $Z$ undergoing a fission reaction and breaking into two daughter nuclei of radii $R_1$ and $R_2$ as shown in figure below. We define the mass ratio of fission products 1 to 2 as $f$. Assume that mass density and charge density of parent and daughter nuclei are same.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/inpho-2014-7-fig1.png

(a) [1 mark] Estimate the nuclear mass density ($\rho_n$) assuming $m_p = m_n$.

(b) [1 mark] The sum of the surface energies of the fissioned daughter nuclei can be written as $U_A^{\mathrm{d}} = a_S R_0^2\alpha$. Obtain $\alpha$ in terms of $f$.

(c) [1 mark] Obtain the total electrostatic energy $U_E^{\mathrm{p}}$ of parent nuclei in terms of given parameters and relevant universal constants.

(d) [1 mark] Calculate $U_E^{\mathrm{p}}$ (in MeV) in terms of $Z$ and $A$ only.

(e) [2 marks] i. Obtain the total electrostatic energy $U_E^{\mathrm{d}}$ of daughter nuclei just after the fission i.e. at the instance shown in Fig. (b).

ii. $U_E^{\mathrm{d}}$ can be simplified and written in terms of $U_E^{\mathrm{p}}$ i.e. in terms of electrostatic energy of parent nucleus as $U_E^{\mathrm{d}} = \beta U_E^{\mathrm{p}}$ where $\beta$ depends solely on $f$. Obtain $\beta$.

(f) [3 marks] Surface energy calculation

i. Energy $Q$ released in fission is described as the difference in energy between the instances shown in Fig. (a) and Fig. (c) i.e. parent nuclei and product nuclei separated by a very large distance. Obtain the expression for $a_S$ in terms of $\{Q\,(\text{inMeV}), Z, A, \alpha, \gamma\}$, where $A$ and $Z$ refer to the parent nucleus. Here $\gamma$ depends solely on $f$.

ii. Assuming that the above expression holds, calculate $a_S$ (in units of $\mathrm{MeV/fm^2}$) for the following reaction with $Q$ value $173.2\,\mathrm{MeV}$:

$$ {}^{1}_{0}n + {}^{235}_{92}\mathrm{U} \rightarrow {}^{141}_{56}\mathrm{Ba} + {}^{92}_{36}\mathrm{Kr} + 3\left({}^{1}_{0}n\right)$$

(g) [1½ marks] General $Z^2/A$ limit

Condition for fission to occur can be expressed as $\dfrac{Z^2}{A} > C$ where $C$ depends on $a_S$ and $f$. Obtain $C$.

(h) [2½ marks] Assume that $a_S$ is a constant function of $f$, using the value of $a_S$ obtained in part f(ii), calculate the minimum value of $C$.

problems.title: Question 6: The Yukawa Potential and the nucleus
problems.problem:
[12 marks]

$\textbf{The Yukawa Potential and the nucleus}$

In 1935 the Japanese physicist Hideki Yukawa proposed that the strong attractive central potential binds the proton and the neutron with the associated potential energy $U(r)$ where

$$U(r) = -g^2\,\frac{e^{-r/\lambda}}{r}$$

where $\lambda = \hbar/m_\pi c$, with $m_\pi$, being the pion mass $= 138.00\,\mathrm{MeV/c^2}$ and $r$ is the distance between nucleons. Here $g^2$ is the nuclear force constant. Our task is to determine the numerical value of nuclear force constant $g^2$. For simplicity we assume that the proton and the neutron in the deuteron have equal masses, $m_{\mathrm{p}} = m_{\mathrm{n}} = m = 938.00\,\mathrm{MeV/c^2}$. Here subscript n,p refers to neutron and proton respectively (see figure below). They are in circular motion under the influence of $U(r)$ about their centre of mass (CM) and their ground state binding energy ($E_b$) is $2.22\,\mathrm{MeV}$.

This two mass problem can be reduced to that of a single mass namely effective mass $\mu = m_{\mathrm{p}}/2$ in CM frame with velocity $\bar{v} = \bar{v_{\mathrm{n}}} - \bar{v_{\mathrm{p}}}$ where $|\bar{v_{\mathrm{n}}}| = |\bar{v_{\mathrm{p}}}|$. The $\textbf{total}$ angular momentum of the n-p pair is quantized as per the Bohr quantization formula.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/inpho-2016-6-fig1.png

In what follows, express numerical values of energy in MeV ($1\,\mathrm{MeV} = 1.6\times10^{-13}\,\mathrm{J}$) and length in fm ($1\,\mathrm{fm} = 10^{-15}\,\mathrm{m}$), mass in $\mathrm{MeV/c^2}$ and related quantities in terms of these.

(a) [½ mark] Calculate $\lambda$.

(b) [1 mark] State the total energy $E$ of the deuteron in terms of $\{\mu, r\}$ and relevant quantities.

(c) [1½ marks] Relate the centripetal force on $\mu$ to $U(r)$.

(d) [1 mark] State the magnitude of the total angular momentum $L$ about the CM.

(e) [2 marks] Obtain the expression for $n^{th}$ energy level ($E_n$) of deuteron in terms of $g^2$ and $r_n$, where $r_n$ is the radius of corresponding circular orbit.

(f) [2 marks] Consider the ground state of the deuteron ($n = 1$). Define $x_1 = r_1/\lambda$. Here $r_1$ is the radius of first orbit of deuteron. Obtain a polynomial equation of $x_1$ involving only fundamental constants and $E_b$.

(g) [2 marks] Estimate $x_1$ numerically. Also calculate the radius of first orbit i.e. $r_1$.

(h) [2 marks] Obtain the nuclear force constant $g^2$ numerically in units of $\mathrm{MeV\cdot fm}$.

[Constants from the paper's Table of Information: $c = 3.00\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $h = 6.63\times10^{-34}\,\mathrm{J\,s}$.]

Consider a particle of mass $m$ confined to a one dimensional box of length $L$. The particle moves in the box with momentum $p$ colliding elastically with the walls. We consider the quantum mechanics of this system. As far as possible, express your answers in terms of $\alpha = h^2/8m$.

(a) [1] At each energy state, the particle may be represented by a standing wave given by the de Broglie hypothesis. Express its wavelengths $\lambda_{\mathrm{dB}}$ in terms of $L$ in the $n^{\mathrm{th}}$ energy state.

(b) [1] Write the energy of the $n^{\mathrm{th}}$ energy state, $E_n$.

(c) [2] Let there be $N$ (mass $m$) electrons in this box where $N$ is an even number. Obtain the expression for the lowest possible total energy $U_0$ of the system (e.g., the ground state energy of this $N$-particle system). Neglect coulombic interaction between the electrons.

(d) [3½] Express the total energy $U_1$ in terms of $U_0$ and relevant quantities when the system is in the first excited state. Also express the total energy $U_2$ in terms of $U_0$ and relevant quantities when the system is in the second excited state.

(e) [1] When the system is in the ground state, let the length of the box change slowly from $L$ to $L - \Delta L$. Obtain the magnitude of the force $F$ on each wall in terms of $U_0$, when $\Delta L \ll L$.

(f) [1] Assuming $N$ is large ($N \gg 1$) obtain the ratio $r$ of $dU_0/dN$ to the energy level of the highest occupied ground state.

(g) [1½] We assume once again that $N$ is large. Consider the possibility of the electrons forming a uniform continuum of length $L$ with constant linear density. Using dimensional analysis, calculate the gravitational energy of this system $U_{\mathrm{G}}$ assuming that it depends on its total mass, universal gravitational constant $G$ and $L$. Equate this (attractive) energy to the (repulsive) energy $U_0(N)$. Obtain $L$ in terms of $N$ and related quantities.

problems.title: Question 2
problems.problem:
[8 marks] Prof. Saha gave the following problem to four students.

In this problem work done by a system on its surroundings is taken as positive. A non-ideal gas follows the Van der Waals equation of state

$$\left(P + \frac{n^2 a}{V^2}\right)(V - nb) = nRT$$

where $P$, $V$, and $T$ denote the pressure, volume, and temperature, respectively; $n$ is the number of moles; $R$ is the universal gas constant and $a, b$ are dimensional positive constants. This gas expands adiabatically from an initial temperature $T_i$ and volume $V_i$ to a final temperature $T_f$ and volume $V_f$. The adiabatic process is described by an equation of the form $f(P, V; n, a, b, \alpha) = \text{constant}$, where $\alpha$ is a dimensionless number which is greater than 1. It is given that $\alpha \to \gamma$ in the ideal gas limit, where $\gamma$ is the adiabatic exponent. What is the work ($W$) done by the gas in the process?

The four students solved the problem independently and gave four different answers. Their answers were:

(a) $W = \dfrac{nR}{\alpha - 1}(T_i - T_f) + n^2 a\left(V_f^{-1} - V_i^{-1}\right)$

(b) $W = \dfrac{nR}{\alpha - 1}(T_f - T_i) + n^2 a\left(V_f^{-1} - V_i^{-1}\right)$

(c) $W = \dfrac{nR}{\alpha - 1}(T_i - T_f) + n^2 a\left(V_f^{\alpha - 1} - V_i^{\alpha - 1}\right)$

(d) $W = \dfrac{nR}{\alpha - 1}(T_i - T_f)\left[1 - \left(\dfrac{V_f - nb}{V_i - nb}\right)^{\alpha - 1}\right]$

Now, Prof. Saha had actually provided the exact expression of $f(P, V; n, a, b, \alpha)$ to the students, but could not remember it during evaluation. Still, he could determine that some or all of the four answers above must be incorrect, based on general physical arguments alone.

Consider each of the four answers and give at least one reason for each of them showing why it is wrong, or possibly correct. Note that you are not required to give a correct expression for $W$ or a detailed derivation for it in this question.

problems.title: Question 3: Chandrayaan-3
problems.problem:
On July 14, 2023, India's lunar mission satellite, Chandrayaan-3, was successfully launched by the Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO). Chandrayaan-3 (mass $m = 3900\,\mathrm{kg}$) was taken to the Moon through a series of Earth Bound Manoeuvres (elliptical) orbits (EBNs) as depicted in the figure below. In this problem, we will explore the physics governing some part of its journey, employing a simplified model. For all parts of this problem except part (f), we consider Chandrayaan-3 to be moving only under the influence of Earth's gravity (a central force).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/inpho-2024-3-fig1.jpg

[From the table of constants of the paper: $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{N\cdot m^{2}\cdot kg^{-2}}$; Earth's radius $R_E = 6371\,\mathrm{km}$; Earth's mass $M_E = 5.97\times10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}$; Moon's mass $M_M = 7.35\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{kg}$; Moon's radius $R_M = 1737\,\mathrm{km}$.]

(a) [6 marks] Upon launch, Chandrayaan-3 entered an elliptical orbit around Earth, with Earth at one of the foci (E) as shown below. The points P and A are the perigee (nearest point from the Earth) and apogee (farthest point from the Earth), respectively. We introduce the polar coordinate system $(r,\theta)$, where $\vec{r}$ is the vector from the centre of the Earth (origin) to the satellite, and $\theta$ is the angle that $\vec{r}$ makes with the major axis (PA $= 2a$). https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/inpho-2024-3-fig2.png

The equation of the ellipse can be written in polar coordinates as

$$r = \frac{r_0}{(1 - e\cos\theta)}$$

where $e$ is eccentricity of the orbit ($0 < e < 1$) and $r_0$ is called the latus rectum.

The velocity $\vec{v}$ of the satellite in polar coordinates can be written as

$$\vec{v} = v_r\hat{r} + v_t\hat{\theta} = \dot{r}\hat{r} + r\dot{\theta}\hat{\theta}$$

where $v_r = \dot{r}$ is the "radial" speed and $v_t = r\dot{\theta}$ is the "tangential" speed.

(b) [1.5 marks] Obtain an expression for the total energy ($E$) of the orbiting satellite in terms of $a$ and other constants.

(c) [1 marks] Plot the kinetic energy (KE) of the satellite as a function of $\theta$ over one full orbit. Mark any significant points in terms of $a, e$, and other variables.

Here, the distances are calculated from the surface of the Moon. problems.title: Question 1: The Flywheel Chronicles

A massless string, attached to a point mass $m$ is wound tightly in $n$ turns (without overlap) on the axle. problems.title: Question 2: Gearminator: Rise of the Machines
problems.problem:
We consider a "thought experiment" involving a DC motor and a DC generator coupled mechanically through a gearbox, operating under idealized conditions, to explore the power output and efficiency of the system (see schematic figure below). The schematic gearbox assembly is also shown in the figure.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/inpho-2025-2-fig1.png

Both the motor and the generator have $N$ loops of area $A$ and rotate in a uniform magnetic field of strength $B$. As usual, both the motor and the generator use commutators (indicated by the blue blocks) to reverse the direction of current in each arm every half cycle, to ensure unidirectional output. The generator is connected to an external resistance $R$, and the motor is driven by a constant voltage $V_M$ with an internal resistance $r$. The gearbox is idealized, with no energy loss due to friction or otherwise, and no slipping between the teeth of the gears. For a pair of meshing gears, as shown above, the angular speed ratio, also known as the gear ratio $X$, is defined as:

$$X = \frac{\omega_M}{\omega_G},$$

where $\omega_M$ and $\omega_G$ are the angular velocities of the motor and the generator, respectively. Let $\langle P_G\rangle$, and $\langle P_M\rangle$ be the time-averaged generator output power and the time-averaged motor input power, respectively, over one complete cycle.

(a) [6 marks] Derive the expression for $\omega_G$ in terms of $X$, $R$, $r$, and the given parameters. For fixed values of $r$ and $R$, determine the expression of $X$ for which $\omega_G$ is maximum.

(b) [3 marks] Derive the expression for the generator output power $\langle P_G\rangle$ in terms of $X$, $R$, $r$, and the given parameters. For fixed values of $r$ and $R$, determine the expression of $X$ for which $\langle P_G\rangle$ is maximum.

(c) [5 marks] For fixed values of $r$ and $R$, determine the condition on $X$ for which the efficiency $\eta$ is maximum, where

$$\eta = \frac{\langle P_G\rangle}{\langle P_M\rangle}.$$

Calculate this maximum value of $\eta$.

problems.title: Question 5: Metalens
problems.problem:
A metasurface is a two-dimensional, ultra-thin optical structure consisting of an array of nanospaced optical nano-elements (also known as meta-atoms) on a flat surface (typically an ultra-thin glass plate). The primary function of the nano-elements is to locally introduce a phase shift $\phi\left(\vec{\mathbf{r}}\right)$ to the wave, incident at position $\vec{\mathbf{r}}$. This function, $\phi\left(\vec{\mathbf{r}}\right)$, is called the phase profile of the metasurface.

Metalens has a circular metasurface with a circularly symmetric phase profile function, $\phi(r)$, which depends on the distance $r$ of the point from the center of the metalens (see figure below). This type of metalens can be used for focusing incoming parallel rays to a point. Unlike normal lenses, the metalens will look just like an ultrathin circular disc.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/inpho-2025-5-fig1.png

Consider two homogeneous media of refractive indices $n_1$ and $n_2$ separated by a metalens as shown in the figure below. Suppose a beam of plane wave is incident at point $Q$ (at distance $r$ from the pole $P$) on the metasurface at an angle of $\theta_1$ from medium 1. Assume that the rays falling at $Q$ are in the plane containing $PQ$ and the axis of the lens ($x$-$z$ plane). These rays will be refracted at an angle $\theta_2$ in the medium 2. The angle of refraction $\theta_2$ depends on $r$. Thus, the modified law of refraction for the metasurface can be written as

$$n_1 \sin\theta_1 - n_2 \sin\theta_2 = f\left(r\right)$$

Similarly, the rays falling at $Q'$, at a distance $r'$, will be refracted by an angle $\theta_2'$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/inpho-2025-5-fig2.png

(a) [8 marks] Find $f(r)$ in terms of $\phi(r)$ and $k_o$, the wave number of the incoming wave in a vacuum. To determine $f(r)$, assume two rays in $x$-$z$ plane incident at an angle $\theta_1$ at two infinitesimally close points, $r$ and $r + \Delta r$, are refracted by the same angle $\theta_2$. You don't need to derive the exact functional form of $\phi(r)$ for this part.

(b) [4 marks] Derive an expression for the phase profile $\phi(r)$, to convert a plane wavefront to spherical wavefront, with light being focused to a point $F$ on the axis (see figure below), which is at a distance $f$ from the pole P.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/inpho-2025-5-fig3.png
